findings.title: New Buttons rely on implicit variants or sizes
findings.why_it_matters: The refactor does not fully satisfy its own action-component contract because several new production Button usages inherit defaults instead of declaring both props. That makes these customer and admin actions change implicitly if the shared Button defaults change, which is exactly the drift the new design contract is intended to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: Add explicit variant and size props to the retry Button, both cancel-dialog Buttons, the mobile language Buttons, and TimePill; use the existing default values where no visual change is intended.
evidence: DESIGN.md:60 requires: `actions: explicit Button variant and size`.
src/app/admin/(dashboard)/orders/error.tsx:35 adds `<Button onClick={reset}>` with neither an explicit variant nor size.
src/components/admin/order-card.tsx:223-229 adds two cancel-dialog Buttons with variants but no explicit size.
src/components/layout/header.tsx:138-146 adds mobile language Buttons with a variant but no explicit size.
src/components/order/order-content.tsx:412-420 replaces the pickup-time control with a Button that declares a variant but no size.

findings.title: Manifest omits shared modified admin components
findings.why_it_matters: DX tooling and future contributors will treat reusable components changed by this refactor as outside the declared design system even though the manifest claims to cover them. `StatStrip` and `MenuItemRow` are both consumed by production admin routes and the shared development preview, so omitting them makes the stated partial-coverage boundary inaccurate.
findings.suggested_fix: Add stable manifest entries for StatStrip and MenuItemRow, then rerun the component-manifest validator.
evidence: docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-refactor-dx-design-conformance-plan.md:92 defines partial coverage as every stable UI file plus shared customer/admin composites modified by this refactor.
.dx/component-manifest.json:6 repeats that coverage claim, but its complete components array at lines 7-42 contains neither StatStrip nor MenuItemRow.
src/app/admin/(dashboard)/page.tsx:7 and src/app/dev/admin/page.tsx:22 both import the modified StatStrip component.
src/app/admin/(dashboard)/menu/page.tsx:7 and src/app/dev/admin/page.tsx:25 both import the modified MenuItemRow component.

findings.title: Opening status still consumes direct palette steps
findings.why_it_matters: The opening-state presentation remains coupled to concrete forest and cream ramp values instead of the semantic roles introduced by this refactor. Future role or contrast changes can therefore update the design system without updating this customer-facing status treatment, leaving opening truth visually inconsistent with the declared token contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the changed forest/cream utilities with existing semantic surface, foreground, border, and status roles; add a narrowly named semantic alias in globals.css only if the existing roles cannot preserve the approved appearance.
evidence: docs/plans/2026-08-15-001-refactor-dx-design-conformance-plan.md:90 states: `Components consume roles, not direct palette steps.`
src/components/brand/open-status.tsx:25 changes the on-forest treatment to `border-forest-8 bg-forest-10 text-cream-1`, all direct palette-step utilities.
src/components/brand/open-status.tsx:34 continues to map the operational open/closed dot directly to `bg-forest-9` and `bg-cream-8` instead of the semantic status roles added in globals.css.

testing_gaps: Authenticated admin mutations remain intentionally unverified because no explicitly seeded non-production Supabase target was supplied; the current browser suite records a gated skip rather than exercising order, menu, category, or settings mutations.
